headword: {適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}
gloss: the right person in the right place

definitions.gloss: the right person in the right place; well-matched assignment
definitions.explanation: The principle of assigning each person to the role that suits their abilities. A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) used constantly in discussions of staffing and team-building.

examples.japanese: {人事|じんじ}は{適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}が{基本|きほん}だ。
examples.english: Personnel decisions come down to putting the right person in the right place.

examples.japanese: {適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}の{配置|はいち}でチームが{強|つよ}くなった。
examples.english: The team grew stronger once everyone was placed where they fit.

examples.japanese: {能力|のうりょく}のある{人|ひと}を{集|あつ}めるだけでなく、{適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}に{配置|はいち}できるかどうかが{管理職|かんりしょく}の{力量|りきりょう}だ。
examples.english: A manager's ability lies not just in gathering capable people but in whether they can place each one where they belong.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}の{人事|じんじ}: staffing that matches people to roles
- {適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}に{配置|はいち}する: to assign people where they fit
- {適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}を{心|こころ}がける: to aim for the right fit

USAGE:
Often used to praise an assignment after the fact ({適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ}だ) as well as to state the principle. It can also soften a reassignment: moving someone out of a role sounds better framed as {適材|てきざい}{適所|てきしょ} than as a demotion.
